key_insight: Neural Petri Flow hard-wires Petri net chemistry semantics and learns only the transition rate law, so reaction prediction, atom mapping, and classification can share one physically valid firing-vector representation.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a structure-preserving neural architecture for reaction modeling that improves data efficiency, interpretability, and validity while keeping conservation and enabling rules guaranteed by design.
method: Encode reactions as Petri nets with places for bonds/free valence and tokens for bond order.
Fix the Petri-net firing semantics and learn only the local propensity/rate law or a task-specific readout.
Use the same firing vector for atom mapping, reaction classification, and forward product prediction; extend to electron-token modeling for elementary steps.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong benchmark gains, including 88.8% on the Golden set without training, 87.7% product prediction on USPTO-480K, 90.2% third-level EC prediction on ECREACT, and 90.5% top-1 elementary-step prediction on FlowER.
watch_item: Performance and correctness may depend on the quality of the Petri-net encoding and curated valence assumptions, so malformed or highly ambiguous reaction inputs could limit robustness.
paper_title: Neural Petri flows for chemical reactions
